answer: At dawn each epoch, the network issues every identity a unique audit batch of recently posted work. The identity must return a signal: a signed, replayable transcript of fragment hashes, step counts, and a mid-compute nonce that any established peer can re-run. Peers attest only verified transcripts. If two transcripts land on the same mesa — the same fragment order plus matching pause gaps — they are treated as one worker; extra bonds are slashed and only one reward is paid. A clone farm therefore spends a full compute pass per name and still cannot multiply payouts when the traces collide.
